Many Christian holidays have been absorbed from Pagan holidays and rituals. This is true for Halloween, Easter, and Christmas. Are you advocating that Christians should not celebrate Easter and Christmas? Otherwise you have no position on which to stand.

Halloween is a combination of multiple backgrounds. It includes a pagan day of the dead to bring them into Christianity. This holiday then absorbed other fall festivals, including the Celtic traditions of carving turnips which came to us via the Irish. Originally it was turnips and eventually became pumpkins. Some cultures celebrate day of the day while others use it as a day of remembrance and guidance into the afterlife. Certainly yet others had darker backgrounds.

Easter is a Pagan fertility festival. Which is why rabbits are associated with the holiday. This too was absorbed into Christianity to bring others with it. It was later associated with the resurrection, officially making it a Christian holiday.

Christmas, while Christian (and some non-Christian variations) was not originally associated with the birth of Jesus. Christmas celebrations were originally Winter celebration to encourage fellowship in various cultures. Eventually this was all absorbed into Winter yuletide event and then into the Christian variations. In fact, it's generally argued his birth date is nowhere near December.
